name: The Stacking Menu Song
why_it_works: A cumulative song adds one item each round and repeats all the earlier ones, so by the end the viewer has heard the first item four times without being sold to. The growing list also builds anticipation: people stay to see how long it gets.

hook.pattern: Sing the first menu item alone, then promise the list keeps growing.
examples: We tried to sing our whole menu.
Every round adds one. Can you keep up?

variables.name: item_one
variables.description: Signature item, lowercase, 2-4 syllables so it sings fast

variables.name: item_four
variables.description: Fourth item or the big closer, lowercase, 2-4 syllables

variables.name: item_one_note
variables.description: What makes the signature item worth ordering, capitalized, 15 words or fewer, true
variables.example: Slow-braised beef, dipped in consomé and crisped on the grill.

variables.name: separate_price
variables.description: The real total for all four items ordered separately

variables.name: offer
variables.description: Reason to order now, capitalized, 8 words or fewer because it is sung

Vertical overhead photo, the same table now with {{item_two}} added beside the {{item_one}}, warm light
Vertical overhead photo, table now holds {{item_three}}, {{item_two}} and {{item_one}}, slightly crowded, hands reaching in
Vertical quick top-down stop-motion style of the full spread filling the table at {{brand}}, plates sliding in to the beat, 9:16

music.feel: playful accordion and guitar polka-pop, steady kick on every beat

slides.body: Four rounds, one more item each time. Sing along.
slides.visual_prompt: Title slide, playful hand-drawn music notes around {{brand}} logo, warm colors

slides.headline: The full lyric
slides.visual_prompt: Full spread overhead, crowded table, joyful mess, lyric space at the top

slides.headline: Why every round ends on {{item_one}}

slides.body: All four ordered separately: {{separate_price}}. Ordered as the song: {{offer}}.

craft.notes: Each round adds one new item at the front and repeats the rest in reverse order, always ending on 'and one {{item_one}}' so the signature item is the resolving title line every time. Keep each item 2-4 syllables and aim each item's stressed syllable at a beat. The track stays at a single tempo (100 BPM, the music.bpm value); each round feels faster because more items are packed into the same bars, so the last round lands like a tongue-twister win. If you want a real speed-up, do it in the edit, not in the music block. Beat seconds are a guide (about ±1s): the edit is cut to the track. Tempo/feel: 100 BPM, accordion, guitar or ukulele strum with a kick on every beat.

do_not: Use more than four items; the joke dies if the viewer can't keep up
Put prices in every round; save the money for the CTA
Copy a known traditional cumulative song's exact tune and words
compliance: Prices on the math slide must match what the register charges, and the offer states when it ends
